newsitem.title: POLAND: POLAND SEES BANK PBK SALE THIS WEEK - ADVISER.
newsitem.headline: POLAND SEES BANK PBK SALE THIS WEEK - ADVISER.

text.p: The Polish authorities will decide this week on an investor for up to 65 percent of Polski Bank Kredytowy SA (PBK), an official from the finance ministry's adviser on the sale, HSBC Investment Services, said.

"I received assurance from ministers that they'll take a decision this week -- I'm counting on Wednesday or Thursday," HSBC's Hubert Janiszewski told Reuters on Tuesday, adding that a contract with the investor should be signed by month's end.
In January the finance ministry invited bids for no less than 10 percent and no more than 65 percent of PBK, with an initial public offer for another 15 percent likely in October.
Janiszewski would not say how many entities had been shortlisted in the tender for the bank which his firm has estimated as having a total value of between 1.2 billion and 1.6 billion zlotys.
A consortium of Polish Development Bank (PBR), Bank Przemyslowo-Handlowy (BPH), Kredyt Bank and insurer Warta has said it submitted a bid for a 51-percent stake in PBK.
Banking sources have said Citibank and South Korea's Samsung were also interested in buying stakes in PBK but neither confirmed the report.
